Score each position of each sequence under a fitted tree

Source: R/likelihood.R
score_positions.Rd

score_positions() returns, for every position of every sequence, the context of the tree that was used to predict it, the state that occurred, the probability the tree gave that state, and its log-likelihood contribution. Low probabilities mark the moves the tree did not expect, which locates where in a sequence it departs from the typical pathways.

With worst, only the positions with the lowest predicted probability are returned, in increasing order of probability. Summed by sequence, the log-likelihood contributions give score_sequences().

Usage

score_positions(tree, newdata, worst = NULL)

Arguments

tree

A transitiontrees object.

newdata

Sequences to score, in any form accepted by context_tree().

worst

Number of least expected positions to return. NULL (default) returns all positions, in sequence order.

Value

A data.frame with one row per scored position and columns sequence_id, position, matched_context (the context used for the prediction; "(start)" for the root), observed (the state that occurred), predicted_prob (its probability) and log_lik (its natural logarithm).

Conditions

transitiontrees_bad_input when tree is not a fitted tree, worst is not a single positive number, or newdata has no usable sequence.

See also

score_sequences(), predict.transitiontrees(), plot_predictive().

Examples

tree <- context_tree(trajectories, max_depth = 2)
score_positions(tree, engagement, worst = 5)
#>   sequence_id position  matched_context   observed predicted_prob   log_lik
#> 1           1       18 Active -> Active Disengaged     0.02078522 -3.873513
#> 2           2       22 Active -> Active Disengaged     0.02078522 -3.873513
#> 3           3       12 Active -> Active Disengaged     0.02078522 -3.873513
#> 4           4       21 Active -> Active Disengaged     0.02078522 -3.873513
#> 5           5        3 Active -> Active Disengaged     0.02078522 -3.873513
